{{Short description|Sporadic simple group}}
{{for|general background and history of the Conway sporadic groups|Conway group}}
{{DISPLAYTITLE:Conway group Co<sub>1</sub>}}
{{Group theory sidebar |Finite}}

In the area of modern algebra known as [[group theory]], the '''Conway group''' ''Co<sub>1</sub>'' is a [[sporadic simple group]] of [[Order (group theory)|order]]
:&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;4,157,776,806,543,360,000
: = 2<sup>21</sup>{{·}}3<sup>9</sup>{{·}}5<sup>4</sup>{{·}}7<sup>2</sup>{{·}}11{{·}}13{{·}}23
: ≈ 4{{e|18}}.

==History and properties==
''Co<sub>1</sub>'' is one of the 26 sporadic groups and was discovered by [[John Horton Conway]] in 1968.  It is the largest of the three sporadic Conway groups and can be obtained as the quotient of ''Co<sub>0</sub>'' ([[Automorphism group|group of automorphisms]] of the [[Leech lattice]] Λ that fix the origin) by its [[center of a group|center]], which consists of the scalar matrices ±1.  It also appears at the top of the automorphism group of the even 26-dimensional unimodular lattice [[II25,1|II<sub>25,1</sub>]]. Some rather cryptic comments in Witt's collected works suggest that he found the Leech lattice and possibly the order of its automorphism group in unpublished work in 1940.

The [[outer automorphism group]] is trivial and the [[Schur multiplier]] has order 2.

==Involutions==
Co<sub>0</sub> has 4 conjugacy classes of involutions; these collapse to 2 in Co<sub>1</sub>, but there are 4-elements in Co<sub>0</sub> that correspond to a third class of involutions in Co<sub>1</sub>.

An image of a dodecad has a centralizer of type 2<sup>11</sup>:M<sub>12</sub>:2, which is contained in a maximal subgroup of type 2<sup>11</sup>:M<sub>24</sub>.

An image of an octad or 16-set has a centralizer of the form 2<sup>1+8</sup>.O{{su|a=c|b=8|p=+}}(2), a maximal subgroup.

== Representations ==

The smallest faithful permutation representation  of Co<sub>1</sub> is on the 98280 pairs {''v'',–''v''} of norm 4 vectors.

The double cover Co<sub>0</sub> has a 24 dimensional representation; when reduced modulo 2, this becomes a representation of the simple group Co<sub>1</sub>. The exterior square and symmetric tensor square of the 24 dimensional representation have dimension 276 and 299, respectively; in characteristic not 2, the former is the smallest faithful representation of the simple group Co<sub>1</sub>.

The centralizer of an involution of type 2B in the [[monster group]] is of the form 2<sup>1+24&thinsp;·</sup>Co<sub>1</sub>. Under this subgroup, the 196883 dimensional representation of the monster reduces as follows: the 24x4096=98304 representation of 2<sup>1+24&thinsp;·</sup>Co<sub>1</sub>, the 98280 dimensional representation of 2<sup>24&thinsp;·</sup>Co<sub>1</sub>, and the 299 dimensional representation of Co<sub>1</sub>.

The Dynkin diagram of the even Lorentzian [[unimodular lattice]] [[II1,25|II<sub>1,25</sub>]] is isometric to the (affine) Leech lattice Λ, so the group of diagram automorphisms is split extension Λ,Co<sub>0</sub> of affine isometries of the Leech lattice.
